meta.title: United Federation of Kadaym · Stellar Atlas

makor.name: Jurah Makor
makor.subtitle: The home of Kadaym
makor.description: The imperial heartland around Mahanzk. Eighteen systems follow the regional chart, with Varkesh Abyss and Vezhkar Pulsar in its outer reaches. Together with adjacent Jurah Lendor it forms the Federation’s central seat. Auvik and Dovrel occupy the outer heartland.

lendor.name: Jurah Lendor
lendor.subtitle: The first expansion
lendor.description: The Federation’s second-largest region by population. Eighteen systems follow the regional chart; Tazhvek Variable lies near its outer edge. Ozhvar Pulsar occupies its northern outer reach. Jurah Makor and Jurah Lendor together form the Federation’s central seat.

narthezk.name: Narthezk
narthezk.subtitle: The acquired territories
narthezk.description: An acquired territory enclosing the Turahk homeworld at Haktur. Eleven settled systems surround its earlier chart, while the Maw and Kharveth Magnetar occupy the outer reaches.

frontier.name: Drayson Hinterlands
frontier.subtitle: Elysian Collective territory · Prathia foothold
frontier.description: A separate inset of the Elysian Collective’s Drayson Hinterlands. Prathia in the Kevak system is the Kadaymian foothold; the surrounding region is not Federation territory. Independent Montressor remains outside Collective control at the rimward edge. Local system positions follow the regional chart; distance and bearing from the heartland are unspecified.
frontier.mapSubtitle: Elysian Collective · Prathia is the Kadaymian foothold

valteo.name: Valteo
valteo.subtitle: The inherited imperial marches
valteo.description: A compact Kadaymian region assembled from the broken western dominions of the Oskalen Empire. Four of its five systems were acquired with their old ports, estates and imperial obligations intact; Khevrin is the Federation’s newer logistical addition. Xai is the regional capital system, and Histekka its capital world. Imperial roadsteads now serve Federation fleets, while rival charter houses still argue over who owns the machinery that keeps them running.

tserazk-makai.name: Tserazk Makai
tserazk-makai.subtitle: Kurzenzka Sector · Silent occupation
tserazk-makai.description: A Silent-infested Kurzenzka sector whose six surveyed systems run from quarantined remnants to critical strongholds. Three stars have been blackened by the Silent; their worlds endure in a cold, artificial twilight. The Federation retains claims and distant observation lines, not effective control. No tier here means safe passage. At KRZ-147, Nefmaat has made no observed maneuver beyond its slow orbit for over eighty years.

drezhvahl.name: Drezhvahl
drezhvahl.subtitle: Western approaches
drezhvahl.description: Freighters approaching Jurah Makor from the west cross Drezhvahl. The outer survey routes converge at Orzheld.

ildovahr.name: Ildovahr
ildovahr.subtitle: Northern approaches to Makor
ildovahr.description: Ildovahr borders Jurah Makor to the south. The old Drakkon route reaches the heartland here.

krevach.name: Krevach
krevach.subtitle: Southwestern escarpment
krevach.description: Southwestern escarpment. The Vekhar Cordon seals the adjoining orbits of Rettan, Dreivar. Traffic elsewhere in the region stays outside the perimeter. Its chart is oriented relative to the paired heartlands of Jurah Makor and Jurah Lendor.

daurovna.name: Daurovna
daurovna.subtitle: Former Triax Confederacy
daurovna.description: Daurovna follows the territory of the former Triax Confederacy. Trilaria Stellaris anchors its inner border with Jurah Lendor. Kadaym took Trilaria Prime and Moon Beta in 116 CE. Federation charts retain the local names of the conquered systems and worlds.

velkharn.name: Velkharn
velkharn.subtitle: The northeastern fork
velkharn.description: The northeastern fork. The Odrava Cordon seals the adjoining orbits of Tellen, Korlun. Traffic elsewhere in the region stays outside the perimeter. Its chart is oriented relative to the paired heartlands of Jurah Makor and Jurah Lendor.

orravai.name: Orravai
orravai.subtitle: Western marches
orravai.description: Orravai follows the western rim between Drezhvahl and Krevach.

kharnevik.name: Kharnevik
kharnevik.subtitle: Southeastern containment district
kharnevik.description: Six black holes account for half of Kharnevik’s charted systems. Several have no catalogued planets. Pilots crossing between the settled worlds use lensing tables to identify the dark primaries against the background stars. The Khevrad Cordon encloses Daumir, Drevau and the Yovrek black hole. The other five black holes lie outside the quarantine.

uldrei-vahr.name: Uldrei Vahr
uldrei-vahr.subtitle: Kurzenzka Sector · Silent occupation
uldrei-vahr.description: A broken crescent beyond Drezhvahl. Ore trains still cross its inner systems under Silent control. At the old frontier, the last Federation beacon transmits a warning and no return vector.

kezhrava.name: Kezhrava
kezhrava.subtitle: Kurzenzka Sector · Silent occupation
kezhrava.description: A compact Kurzenzka sector beyond Ildovahr. Silent foundries occupy the first system. In the second, a darkened star backlights the long filaments connecting its assembly yards. Federation patrols monitor both from outside the perimeter.

systems.name: Xai
systems.description: Capital system of Valteo and the former western seat of the Oskalen Empire. Its surviving customs rings, ceremonial docks and oath archives were acquired largely intact. Histekka now houses the regional administration; imperial charter houses compete to supply the same fleets they once resisted.

notableSites.name: Vezhka Keelworks

systems.name: Zhorel
systems.description: An acquired archival system of the former Oskalen Empire. The dry basins of Azhmera hold registries of tribute, bloodline and ship ownership. Kadaymian examiners and old custodial families have spent decades reconciling mutually incompatible claims.

notableSites.name: Azhmera
notableSites.summary: Ancient vaults and automated toll contracts survive authorities that vanished long ago.

notableSites.name: Zhevara Record House
notableSites.summary: An orbital archive where visiting crews may discover their vessels belong to a supposedly extinct charter.

systems.name: Vadrask
systems.description: The heavy forge system inherited with Valteo. Its orbital works can still cast hull sections to imperial patterns whose original specifications have vanished. Old industrial houses hold useful technical monopolies, despite the Federation’s nominal ownership.

systems.name: Oltzheim
systems.description: An acquired agricultural system whose reservoir estates and refrigerated freight vaults once provisioned the imperial court. The Federation retained the machinery and the growers; ownership of the oldest water charters is still bitterly disputed.

systems.name: Khevrin
systems.description: Valteo’s one substantial post-acquisition addition: a Federation supply system built around Thozhvek. New transit yards bypass the hereditary fees of the older ports, making Khevrin commercially successful and deeply unpopular with the surviving charter houses.

systems.name: KRZ-114
systems.description: A quarantined outer system with scattered Silent remnants. Empty relay shelters still receive obsolete purge codes; a distant Federation observation line watches for renewed activity.

systems.name: KRZ-118
systems.description: Suppressed but never cleared. Dormant drones lie beneath the wrecks of a refinery belt, and brief power signatures recur in buildings that have been cold for generations.

systems.name: KRZ-126
systems.description: An active Silent mining system. Uncrewed haulers feed an automated defense lattice assembled through the ruins of the old orbital economy.

systems.name: KRZ-133
systems.description: A heavily contaminated dead system. The Silent have blackened Zherak’s star; automated factories continue to work around frozen Zhereth, drawing power from sources that no longer appear stellar.

notableSites.name: Zhereth
notableSites.summary: A frozen industrial world beneath a Silent-darkened star, its orbital works alive with unfamiliar red activity.

notableSites.name: Zhereth Crown Ruins
notableSites.summary: Isolated modules of a collapsed inhabited ring still transmit identification calls.

systems.name: KRZ-147
systems.description: A critical Silent stronghold around a blackened star. Nefmaat, a Nefandum-class shipbreaker, has remained on the same slow orbit for over eighty years without any observed maneuver. Its stillness is not treated as evidence of dormancy.

notableSites.name: Nefmaat
notableSites.summary: The motionless shipbreaker has made no observed maneuver beyond its slow stellar orbit for over eighty years.

notableSites.name: Ozhmera
notableSites.summary: Remote probes detect periodic signals from the empty foundations of its broken navigation temples.

notableSites.name: Ozhmak Processional Wrecks
notableSites.summary: Shattered transports share an uncanny orientation, as though interrupted during the same maneuver.

systems.name: KRZ-151
systems.description: The sector’s deepest surveyed dead system. A nearly continuous web of Silent structures surrounds the dark star. Reconnaissance returns are sparse; most identifiable debris belongs to vanished purge fleets.

systems.name: Vaurzhek
systems.description: The Vaurzhek black hole is usually visible only when it lenses the dense starfield behind it. The first reliable mass estimate came from two surveys made eleven years apart.

systems.name: Othreln
systems.description: A narrow stream of dust feeds Othreln from the equatorial plane of its surviving debris belt. Veldrau and its moon pass well outside the bright inner disk.

systems.name: Kelvair
systems.description: Kelvair has a thin, intermittent accretion disk. Cartographers fixed its position from the repeating split image of a distant binary.

systems.name: Drezhun
systems.description: Drezhun bends the light from stars along the old crossing to Revik. Pilots use a pair of reference stars well clear of the distorted field.

systems.name: Irvauk
systems.description: Irvauk holds a single catalogued ice giant in a wide orbit. Its moon supplied the first long baseline for measuring the mass of the unseen primary.

systems.name: KRZ-162
systems.description: Silent haulers follow a regular circuit between the inner rubble fields and the stripped industrial world of Ozhrehn.

systems.name: KRZ-168
systems.description: The star has gone dark. Federation surveyors tracked a convoy by the silhouettes it cut across background stars before its escorts turned toward the probe.

systems.name: KRZ-175
systems.description: The outer orbit is littered with broken mirror arrays. Silent harvesters retrieve the fragments that still hold a reflective coating.

systems.name: KRZ-183
systems.description: Foundries on Vekhra send billets into orbit in pulses. Long-range observers can time shift changes from the intervals between launches.

systems.name: KRZ-189
systems.description: The Silent have blackened the star. Long filaments draw material from the orbit of Azhrun into assembly yards that radiate most strongly in the far infrared.

Mahanzk.description: The heart of the Federation and home of the Kadaymian species. The great Makal storm dominates the world, while Kurzk houses the seat of imperial power. Its location is concealed from the Elysian Collective.

Helkana.description: The largest and most developed world of the Garden Arc. Much of the surface is protected agricultural land and nature reserve; most residents inhabit moving, airborne Navistad cities.

Vardis Prime.description: A vast industrial and manufacturing world, with the Federation’s largest human population. Its densely built cities supply military equipment, advanced machinery and spacecraft components.

Rakazk.description: An arid, rugged world beneath the dim light of Drelkov. Isolated settlements, metallurgy company towns and renowned Rahmara temples share this difficult frontier.

Zekozha.description: A glacial mining world whose cavern-cities are warmed by geothermal activity. Rich Naydor deposits made it an economic powerhouse despite the bitter cold.

Qerzhek.description: A populous world of frozen seas, glaciers and small landmasses. Its residents celebrate seasonal changes around the icy oceans with drink and festivals.

Prathia.description: An annexed Kadaym world in the Drayson Hinterlands. Annexed in 129 CE, Prathia acquired the Kahenzi name Palorek, “Gateway.” The Kevak jumpgates were destroyed during the CONCORD blockade.

Ysh Kha’lah.description: The Turahk homeworld in conquered Narthezk. The controlled-worlds register places it in Haktur and records acquisition on 7 Veritas, 100 CE. No regional chart or further system position is supplied.

Zelenzk.description: Zelenzk, the Lunar Mother, is the primary moon of Mahanzk and a naturally habitable world. Its ancient colonies predate the Near-End, and it holds particular significance for the Moonbloods.

Keyhaul Trench.description: The Karkarian homeworld is an oceanic planet in the Drayson system, with scattered archipelagos and island chains. Its article places it fourth from its primary.

Varkhuz.description: A compact, airless world of dark basalt and exposed metal, marked by long fractures across its rust-colored crust.

Kezhrin.description: A pale dwarf world beneath a hard shell of ancient ice. Dark mineral seams break through its frost-covered surface.

Ozhrevik.description: A dim violet gas giant encircled by thin, broken rings. Its broad outer orbit shelters a scatter of cold satellite fragments.

Narvokh.description: A dense, irregularly weathered planetoid with bare iron-rich ridges and almost no atmosphere.

Thezkar.description: A battered ochre world crossed by bright fault lines. Loose debris follows its orbit around the Maw.

Ulzheim.description: A cold blue-gray giant whose narrow rings are threaded with dark rubble from older satellite collisions.

Vezhrak.description: A charcoal-colored inner body with a patchwork of glassy impact plains and sharp, unweathered craters.

Khorveth.description: A remote icebound world with a blue-white surface, deep shadowed clefts and a tenuous veil of frozen volatiles.

Zarnovek.description: A muted amber giant with a broad, tilted ring system, marking the outermost named orbit of the Vezkarn Singularity.

Tribaven.description: Tribaven is a Kadaymian world in the Vezeir system. Its small outer moon Trevik follows a solitary orbit.

Histekka.description: Capital planet of Valteo. Cool inland seas divide stepped basalt cities and long, roofed processional roads. In Haarzen, the former imperial chancery now houses a Federation governor beneath sealed upper galleries; the old court’s archives, family lodges and service tunnels remain a city within the city.

Enzhal.description: A small scorched inner world cut by copper-colored rifts. Imperial mirror furnaces along its terminator have been retooled for specialized alloys, although sealed descent shafts beneath the oldest smelters appear on no surviving plan.

Orvetha.description: A pale ringed giant beyond Histekka. Its broad dust bands shelter abandoned royal fuel depots, while modern skimmers service the inhabited ports farther inward. Traffic controllers still use the imperial names for gaps in its rings.

Azhmera.description: A dry world of salt basins and deep archival vaults. The oldest records are stored in ceramic cylinders beneath shuttered observatories; some still collect tolls through automated contracts that no living authority can cancel.

Khelvar.description: A dense industrial planet where black-glass highlands rise above furnace valleys. Whole districts operate as inherited concessions, supplying both Federation shipyards and private charter fleets. The unlit northern foundries are formally closed but continue to consume power.

Varnessa.description: A cool agricultural world of reservoir terraces, long grain belts and storm-sheltered market towns. Its water charters are older than the Federation administration; estate families lease storage, rainfall rights and even thaw schedules.

Thozhvek.description: A gray desert world with a young Federation freight city clustered around deep geothermal wells. Crews arriving from the imperial ports find broad repair yards, plain contracts and a lively trade in machinery with disputed serial numbers.

Vezhret.description: An evacuated settlement world under quarantine. Sealed habitats and surface relay shelters remain largely intact, but scattered Silent remnants make civilian return impossible.

Izhvala.description: A refinery world of dark settling basins and abandoned pressure towns. Suppression patrols periodically disable Silent nodes that reactivate in previously cleared districts.

Rhazva.description: A stripped mining planet where drone columns pass between old open pits and new Silent excavation mouths. The remaining cities are used as raw material.

Zhereth.description: A frozen former industrial world beneath a Silent-darkened star. Habitation towers stand inside advancing ice sheets; the orbital works remain bright with an unfamiliar red activity.

Ozhmera.description: A cold, ash-colored world under the blackened Ozhmak star. Its former navigation temples are broken open, and instruments on remote probes report periodic signals from the empty foundations. Nefmaat’s orbit lies beyond the planet.

Kezhrun.description: A dark world whose nightside is crossed by vast geometric excavations. Its former orbital settlements survive as fragments embedded in Silent structures.

Ferryman’s Rest.description: A 142,500 km gas ice giant in the fifth orbital position around MAKOR-9*. Ammonia clouds and silicate dust trace blue-gray bands across its atmosphere. The inhabited infrastructure is in orbit, where thirteen stations serve industrial and naval operations.

Kaldana III.description: The third planet of the Kaldana system. Salem Cross Station was built in orbit here to extract and refine ore.

stations.name: Kurzk Highworks
stations.description: An orbital civil works yard assembling habitat sections, repairing lift infrastructure and dispatching construction tugs.

stations.name: Zhelvakh Habitat
stations.description: A rotating garden habitat serving lunar families, pilgrims and long-stay visitors.

stations.name: Virezk Fleet Bastion
stations.description: A fleet anchorage with command berths, repair docks and training facilities.

stations.name: Kurzheit Orbital Battery
stations.description: A fixed defensive platform guarding the inner system’s approach corridors.

stations.name: Makor Foundry Ring
stations.description: A vacuum foundry and orbital fabrication complex supplying shipyards and heavy construction.

stations.name: Velkhor Observatory
stations.description: A quiet deep-space observatory and archive for stellar weather records.

stations.name: Helkana Watershed Array
stations.description: A monitoring and logistics station supporting water management and planetary infrastructure.

stations.name: Talrensk Residential Cylinder
stations.description: A residential cylinder with parkland promenades and views of the system’s two reported primaries.

stations.name: Talrion Listening House
stations.description: A civilian radio observatory and communications relay.

stations.name: Venta Drydock
stations.description: A modular shipbuilding yard producing civilian freighters and orbital construction craft.

stations.name: Lokuz Watch
stations.description: A patrol base coordinating escorts and search-and-rescue deployments.

stations.name: Vardis Commonwheel
stations.description: An inhabited rotating wheel with markets, schools and temporary quarters for dock crews.

stations.name: Rakazk Forge Anchorage
stations.description: A smelting and refitting complex supporting the industrial world below.

stations.name: Kalkov Shield
stations.description: A defensive station assigned to protect the outer approach to the inhabited system.

stations.name: Zarnograd Works Depot
stations.description: A public engineering depot storing prefabricated bridges, utility modules and emergency shelters.

stations.name: Grovazk Skyport
stations.description: An orbital cargo interchange for planetary construction and major public infrastructure.

stations.name: Tezzar Lantern
stations.description: A navigation beacon, astronomical clock and rescue coordination post.

stations.name: Zekozha Gardenwheel
stations.description: A residential habitat with agricultural terraces and passenger accommodation.

stations.name: Jeiho Exchange
stations.description: An orbital sorting and processing hub for bulk cargo and recovered materials.

stations.name: Oðal Garrison
stations.description: A fleet support base with barracks, patrol tenders and replenishment berths.

stations.name: Qerzhek Sentinel
stations.description: A defensive platform protecting traffic near the inhabited world.

stations.name: Haktur Reconstruction Yard
stations.description: A proposed modular depot for infrastructure repair and transport maintenance.

stations.name: Haktur Memory Vault
stations.description: A cultural archive and conservation laboratory preserving records from across the system.

stations.name: Prathia Anchorage
stations.description: A frontier logistics base for patrol craft, supply ships and visiting crews.

stations.name: Gunther Bay Highport
stations.description: An orbital freight terminal and servicing yard connecting planetary exports to passing commerce.

stations.name: Azren Medical Station
stations.description: A neutral-service medical habitat with rescue craft and long-duration recovery wards.

stations.name: Odeijo Transfer Yard
stations.description: A construction and cargo-transfer station supporting the system’s colonies; its placement does not assign either colony an orbit.

stations.name: Izhket Commonhouse
stations.description: A rotating residential habitat and rendezvous for colony traffic.

stations.name: Beithen Seedbank
stations.description: A climate-controlled repository of seed stocks, ecological records and restoration samples.

stations.name: Beithen Materials Works
stations.description: A recycling and fabrication station supplying the system’s inhabited worlds.

stations.name: Salem Cross Station
stations.description: Kisaragi Heavy Industries built this ore extraction and refining station in orbit around Kaldana III. The Sixth Armada declared it condemned after the Silent attack.

stations.name: Circa’s Triad
stations.description: A documented autonomous, neutral site in Columa. Its precise orbital location and specialist station category are unspecified.

stations.name: Shryke Jumpgate
stations.description: A jumpgate named on the regional chart. Its exact location within the system is unspecified.

stations.name: Montressor Station
stations.description: The named station of independent Montressor. Its precise host orbit and specialist category are unspecified.

stations.name: Palorek Bastion
stations.description: The orbital command bastion coordinates the Kevak garrison, patrol deployments and the defense of Prathia.

stations.name: Palorek Arsenal
stations.description: An orbital weaponry depot stores and services munitions for the Palorek defenses and visiting fleet units.

stations.name: Vazhkorr Fleet Yards
stations.description: Orbital engineering yards repair fleet hulls, rebuild damaged infrastructure and assemble replacement station sections.

stations.name: Kevak Outer Picket
stations.description: An outer-system patrol station watches distant approaches and coordinates reconnaissance craft across the Kevak perimeter.

stations.name: Zharvek Interdiction Array
stations.description: A stellar-orbit weapons array controls approach corridors with tracking platforms and overlapping defensive batteries.

stations.name: Palorek Quarantine Station
stations.description: An outer-system military checkpoint isolates suspect vessels and directs quarantine patrols responding to Silent activity.

stations.name: Haarzen Crownport
stations.description: The main highport over Histekka. Imperial reception arms now berth Federation transports; the locked ceremonial quay remains reserved by an obsolete succession charter.

stations.name: Xai Charter Exchange
stations.description: A crowded residential and commercial cylinder over Histekka where charter families, insurers and military purchasing agents negotiate ownership of the inherited empire.

stations.name: Vezhka Keelworks
stations.description: An inhabited lunar-orbit assembly yard serving Vezhka’s shipwright guilds. Several slips retain fixtures sized for imperial vessels no longer in service.

stations.name: Azhevar Watch
stations.description: A Federation watch station in Xai’s outer approaches. Its quiet remit includes monitoring movements between the old royal fuel depots.

stations.name: Zhevara Record House
stations.description: An orbital archive and arbitration house above Azhmera. Visiting crews sometimes discover that their vessels belong to a charter thought extinct centuries ago.

stations.name: Khelvar High Foundry
stations.description: A bank of immense orbital casting bays over Khelvar, still maintained by descendants of the imperial furnace crews.

stations.name: Oltvara Coldvault
stations.description: Refrigerated orbital stores and bulk transfer docks linking Varnessa’s reservoir estates to the region’s older supply contracts.

stations.name: Thozhvek Transit Yard
stations.description: A new Federation freight and repair yard over Thozhvek, built to route supplies around the hereditary tolls of Valteo’s acquired ports.

stations.name: Velkhar Relay Ruins
stations.description: An abandoned communications spindle above Vezhret. Much of its shell survives, but Silent remnants occupy its service cavities.

stations.name: Izhvala Refinery Wreck
stations.description: A broken refinery whose cooling fins shelter dormant Silent drones. Suppression strikes have left most of the structure without pressure or atmosphere.

stations.name: Rhazken Extraction Lattice
stations.description: A Silent processing lattice woven through the former mining docks over Rhazva.

stations.name: Zhereth Crown Ruins
stations.description: The collapsed remains of a large inhabited orbital ring. Most sections are dark; isolated modules continue to transmit identification calls.

stations.name: Ozhmak Processional Wrecks
stations.description: A long band of shattered transports and ceremonial platforms beyond Ozhmera. Their orientation is remarkably consistent, as if all were interrupted during the same maneuver.

stations.name: Kezhral Defensive Web
stations.description: A dense Silent defense network around the dead star, assembled partly from the hulls of lost purge vessels.

stations.name: Station ᚠ9-604 “Silver Moon”
stations.description: Silver Moon directs the collection platforms that harvest the upper atmosphere.

stations.name: Station ᚢ4-112 “Lighthouse”
stations.description: Warships call here regularly. Its power demand exceeds that of an ordinary support station.

stations.name: Station ᚦ7-908
stations.description: Detachments from several armadas rotate through the station. Its suspected rally-point role is unconfirmed.

stations.name: Station ᚨ2-446 “Inner Ring”
stations.description: Inner Ring has extensive shielding and tightly controlled docking.

stations.name: Station ᚱ1-773 “Starlight”
stations.description: Prototype-module convoys and visiting research vessels suggest testing work at Starlight.

stations.name: Station ᚲ6-220 “Stoneforge”
stations.description: Stoneforge stores supplies, refuels ships and services the orbital infrastructure.

stations.name: Station ᚷ8-319
stations.description: Heavy encrypted traffic has prompted speculation about a communications role.

stations.name: Station ᚹ3-521 “Centerpoint”
stations.description: The Navy transfers crews through Centerpoint’s secured docks.

stations.name: Station ᚺ5-907
stations.description: Escorted convoys visit this station. Its rumored command role is unverified.

stations.name: Station ᚾ7-284
stations.description: Numerous smaller installations surround it. Accounts disagree about atmospheric collection and experimental work.

stations.name: Station ᛟ0-261
stations.description: Vertical rings enclose the station, with no obvious entrance. It is also called Station 2-6-1.

stations.name: Station ᛃ4-833
stations.description: Capital ships have been observed undergoing repairs in its docks.

stations.name: Station ᛇ9-400 “Nine-Four”
stations.description: Nine-Four is the largest station. Its alleged connection to the Seventh Armada remains unconfirmed.

stations.name: Quantum Station
stations.description: Triax research facility that orbited one of the Trilarian moons during the conquest of 116 CE. The campaign account leaves the host moon unnamed.

stations.name: Orzheld Transfer Anchorage
stations.description: Bulk freighters leave their deep-orbit tugs here. Pilots from the five settled worlds take the cargoes inward.

stations.name: Kordaun Fleet Exchange
stations.description: Heartland patrols take on fuel, spares and relief crews before heading for the outer regions.

stations.name: Uzhama Treaty Port
stations.description: Delegations and inbound convoys share the old customs berths above Uzhama.

stations.name: Vaudren Interferometer
stations.description: Its long-baseline receivers follow the distortion of background stars behind the black hole.

stations.name: Tevrozh Kiln
stations.description: A vacuum kiln fires replacement heat shields from local silicates.

stations.name: Vidra Lockhouse
stations.description: Two pressure locks let repair crews bring damaged orbital habitats in under tow.

stations.name: Irvakh Packet Dock
stations.description: Mail pilots exchange sealed dispatch canisters during the short dawn-side rendezvous.

stations.name: Ruun Tide Archive
stations.description: Its Triax surveyors keep centuries of tidal observations from instruments on the surface.

stations.name: Ezhkor Ice Yard
stations.description: Cutters unload blocks of volatile ice into shaded storage cradles.

stations.name: Okhreld Listening Buoy
stations.description: An uncrewed receiver logs surface transmissions and sends narrow-beam reports across the cordon.

stations.name: Khelnir Watch
stations.description: An automated watch station records traffic near the evacuated world. No crews are stationed here.

entities.status: No observed maneuver in over 80 years
entities.description: Nefmaat — Kahenzi for “motionless” — is a Nefandum-class Silent shipbreaker in the dead Ozhmak system, now designated KRZ-147. For over eighty years it has made no observed maneuver apart from its slow orbit around the blackened star. Its slender, double-tapered hull sits within a detached twelve-petalled ring. Neither its patience nor its purpose is understood; observers do not interpret stillness as safety.

presentation.notesHTML:
This atlas assembles the known territory of the United Federation of Kadaym, using current Codex articles and regional map images. Campaign reference: 134 CE. Sources consulted 30 October 2026.

How to use the atlas

Drag to pan, scroll or pinch to zoom. Click inside a region to highlight it at the current zoom. Faint names repeat inside the regional boundaries. Select a star for its dossier; double-click its marker to focus its system; select a location’s name to open its Codex page. Search spans all regions, including unplotted worlds. Use + / − to zoom, arrow keys to pan, and 0 to fit the current region when the chart has keyboard focus.

Animated system views

Each selected system displays its named worlds in a compact orbital diagram. Documented orbital positions determine the actual numbered ring: a third planet is drawn on ring 3, with two smaller planets inward of it. Dim, unnamed planets fill gaps in the schematic diagram. The orbit-order strip reads from inner to outer. Asterisks mark named worlds whose orbital position is unspecified. Planetary views show the natural satellite counts recorded in the planet articles, including named moons and catalogue designations for unnamed moons. Only confirmed inhabited moons appear in solar-system view; Zelenzk remains visible around Mahanzk in both views. Select a numbered body to inspect it, or its name to open the Codex. Pause / Play controls the motion, and reduced-motion preferences are respected. Orbital positions shown as numbers come from planet infoboxes; orbital sizes, inclinations, speeds, phases and the ordering of worlds without a known orbital position are schematic. Stations use distinct symbols for Civil Engineering, Habitation, Military, Weaponry, Industry and Other; documented sites with no specialist category are grouped under Other and labelled as unspecified. Existing station and colony host orbits are not inferred: they appear in an unlocated row. Destroyed Salem Cross remains a historical site. Use Focus system to expand the solar system into the main chart, filter station categories, and inspect object dossiers. Return to region (or Escape) restores the regional chart. All station names link to their matching or expected Codex article titles. Reported binary primaries orbit their shared center. Select the central star or either binary member to inspect its own dossier; its name opens its Codex article. Use Focus planet & satellites to inspect a named world’s local moons and stations, and Return to system to step back. Faint asteroid belts can be hidden with the Belts control. Belt placement and stellar motion are schematic. Pulsar emission ribbons twist around a fixed polar axis; magnetars show a much gentler, slower depth shift in their ribbons and magnetic fields. The cataclysmic variable is an accreting white dwarf and donor pair. Stellar effects are slowed schematic illustrations, not measured rotation or outburst periods.

Direct links & widgets

Link straight to a place with a URL fragment such as #Mahanzk, #Virezk or #Jurah%20Lendor. Copy the atlas address to retain the selected location. Use ?region=valteo&view=widget for a regional chart. Add ?planet=Mahanzk&view=widget for the local orbit alone, or ?system=virezk&view=widget for the solar system alone. Widgets hide all atlas panels; their names and symbols still open Codex articles. Focus the diagram and press Space to pause or play. Reduced-motion preferences are respected.

What the map establishes

The Makor chart, Lendor chart and Hinterlands chart establish local system arrangements and listed worlds. This atlas preserves their relative layouts. System points represent whole systems; worlds are listed beneath them and in dossiers.

Spacing between regions and territorial outlines are schematic. The remote frontier is a separate inset. There is no measured navigational scale, route network or implied travel time. The 224-lightyear figure is the Federation’s published territorial span, not a pixel-to-distance conversion. Faint background stars are decoration and do not represent additional named systems.

Colors distinguish Federation systems, neighboring/neutral systems, and hazards/unresolved designations. They do not reproduce an undocumented color legend from the source images. An unnamed world slot does not mean a system is uninhabited. “Named worlds only” includes systems with named stations or other sites.

Regional ownership

Valteo is a compact acquired region of the Federation, centered on Xai and Histekka. Four of its five systems belonged to the former Oskalen Empire. Tserazk Makai, Uldrei Vahr and Kezhrava are Kurzenzka sectors. Red hatching marks the occupied territory. Each KRZ marker shows its local infestation tier. The Drayson Hinterlands belong to the Elysian Collective, with the Kadaymian foothold on Prathia in Kevak and independent Montressor at the rimward edge.

Beyond the chart

Ferryman’s Rest remains unplotted because its location is classified. Open MAKOR-9* from the Unplotted register to inspect its black hole and Ferryman’s Rest. The former unplotted settlements now appear under their host systems. The original unlocated KRZ records remain under Unplotted. The three charted Kurzenzka sectors use KRZ designations. At KRZ-147 in Tserazk Makai, the Nefandum Nefmaat follows a very slow orbit around a blackened star. The article describes 22 systems in the Hinterlands; the image shows 23 labels including independent Montressor.

This is a selective atlas: the Codex’s 200+ controlled worlds, thousands of stations and 31,223 stars are not all individually named. All named locations link to their matching articles or expected article titles, including pages that have not yet been written.
